[Replay code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yxssxn/skilluminati/0affc46618f62d9b497f177178acefb83f63dd02/plugin/skilluminati/realrun.py) [Test disclosure](https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls/153804)

reads.best: Local spatial operations and shared agent/Desktop state make the map a working analysis environment with meaningful geometry and integration tests ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mackydubzz/hermes-mapdesk/eaaea7102e5d6396840850ee968fe46aea025f41/README.md)).
reads.worst: The palette Open command clears the shared workspace through non-atomic writes, so failure or concurrent agent edits can leave a partial reset despite archiving ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mackydubzz/hermes-mapdesk/eaaea7102e5d6396840850ee968fe46aea025f41/README.md)).

reads.best: Memory changes remain reviewable and gated, with evidence checks, secret scans, locking, atomic writes, snapshots, rollback, and a broad regression suite.
reads.worst: The feature is complex and depends on host hooks and session-log integration; the README says the Dashboard has no pinned screenshot URLs, and older hosts may warn on an unknown hook.

reads.best: Memory changes have locks, stale-evidence checks, secret scanning and receipts, with substantial tests for rollback and user requests not to save information. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noblebrown-69/hermes-oneiros/c9bd78835f6388f04b23a9171c331e6270ef2b73/README.md)
reads.worst: Extraction is a regex pass over labeled facts and user assertions, so it cannot deliver general semantic memory consolidation; naming and docs also retain the separate dream-cycle identity. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noblebrown-69/hermes-oneiros/c9bd78835f6388f04b23a9171c331e6270ef2b73/README.md)

reads.best: Concrete impact reports and verified recovery directly improve the safety of an agent working on the user’s files, with parser and snapshot audit suites.
reads.worst: Protection covers terminal calls only, and strict-mode blast_allow measures in the process cwd while its grant is matched by command text alone, so a different workdir can consume a grant for the wrong snapshot.

reads.best: Real request middleware, conservative evidence thresholds, per-sender recall isolation and extensive failure/privacy tests improve Hermes itself through public extension points.
reads.worst: The supplied live benchmark shows no clear savings, and effective routing needs repeated user marks plus a suitable cheaper model on the same provider.

reads.best: Revision-bound jobs, input hashes and stale-approval invalidation integrate a real local media pipeline with Desktop controls and agent tools.
reads.worst: Advanced editing requires optional native packages and separately acquired models, while the pinned status report leaves fresh-install and native Desktop-window acceptance open.

reads.best: User-defined file-to-host routes are enforced in a pre-tool hook with fail-closed errors and extensive tests.
reads.worst: Its static recognizer covers a bounded syntax subset and cannot enforce all network egress.

reads.best: Its [input arbiter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/hermes-templeos/c61d00eb4d36c5e3c7cd57a2985985aed8db42f0/templeos/arbiter.py) serializes human and agent actions and gives the user explicit take-control and hand-back controls over the live guest.
reads.worst: The [documented workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/hermes-templeos/c61d00eb4d36c5e3c7cd57a2985985aed8db42f0/README.md) serves a narrow OS audience, requires separately installed QEMU, and still labels FAT file transfer experimental and macOS untested as a primary host.

reads.best: A full platform adapter with a sender allowlist, the API key declared as a password requires_env and read through Hermes's env helper, https/wss-only enforcement and eight test files.
reads.worst: Every message goes through a third-party paid relay on onrender.com, and the pip install path tells users to append the key to ~/.hermes/.env by hand.

reads.best: Reviewable browser and Swift code combines stateful device handoff, local hand tracking and explicitly armed native input.
reads.worst: It remains a trusted-LAN HTTP prototype with one paired phone, substantial setup and limited hardware coverage.

reads.best: Transactional state, one-use pairing, revision conflict checks and local-only camera processing make the gesture-and-device handoff more than a visual mockup.
reads.worst: This remains a trusted-LAN HTTP prototype with one active artifact and one phone, a small fixed set of tool types and a separate multi-step companion/native setup.

reads.best: It binds actual command exit codes to Git content and rechecks the precise published commit, with real-repository behavioral tests.
reads.worst: The gate is inactive for remote terminal backends, multiplexed profiles and plugin-host isolation, and custom publishing scripts remain outside its bounded shell recognition ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cirwel/hermes-receipts/0dd1a374cc70ce388040f99adc908c7054ed8fa9/__init__.py)).

reads.best: Local evidence tools combine source locators, content-hashed revisions and visible PDF highlights without requiring a hosted search service. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okyssta/hermes-folio/b101110c32b47b7c427204dfce19710d7f400c75/README.md)
reads.worst: Incremental folder scans skip files solely on unchanged modification time, so changed content with preserved timestamps can leave stale evidence until a forced scan. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okyssta/hermes-folio/b101110c32b47b7c427204dfce19710d7f400c75/indexer.py)

reads.best: Bounded, symlink-resistant hashing and superseding context snapshots address stale recall while leaving the existing memory provider available.
reads.worst: Tracks only explicitly registered small files, and unchanged bytes cannot establish that a saved fact was true in the first place.

reads.best: Bounded capture, persistent verification state and image fixtures support a useful feedback loop with an integrated Desktop comparison view.
reads.worst: The automatic baseline only watches write_file and patch on selected extensions, so terminal edits and UI changes in .ts or .js files escape it.

reads.best: Changes where Hermes runs via a backend provider, with tests, CI and the key declared as a secret env var.
reads.worst: Depends on a paid third-party service; the plugin is mostly a client for it.

reads.best: Evidence-based clean/finding/unknown states, broad fixture tests and an integrated Desktop pane turn a host audit into an actionable workflow.
reads.worst: Coverage remains uneven across Linux families, excludes image-layer CVEs, and offers no macOS or Windows support.

reads.best: Per-turn capture, encrypted WALs, host-model judging and project-scoped semantic recall form a distinctive agent-memory workflow with extensive plumbing tests.
reads.worst: The Hermes adapter judges entries in chronological order but passes the flags unchanged to BackwardWalker, which reverses the entries, so asymmetric relevance verdicts retain the wrong memories.

reads.best: A real Hermes approval gate (pre_tool_call plus post_approval_response grants), drafter secrets read via secret_scope, and about 79 tests that use real git repos.
reads.worst: No sandbox (disclosed), agent-chosen timeouts with no cap, git calls without timeouts, and its headline study results rest on recordings not in the repo.

reads.best: Sealed job sessions, tool locks, replay protection and payment-on-delivery accounting give agent commerce a substantive platform implementation.
reads.worst: The default buyer policy spends up to $0.10 without human approval, and the approval gate does not pin the price or recipient later used for signing.

reads.best: A remarkably complete game drawn entirely in code, with netplay, gamepad support, Shadow DOM isolation and a clean destroy() lifecycle.
reads.worst: It has nothing to do with the agent: Hermes Desktop is only the host page, and the 4,300-line plugin.js is a generated build of game/pixel-hermes.html.

reads.best: Quote-gated claims, explicit contested evidence and persisted snapshots turn repeat research into an auditable workflow.
reads.worst: adapters/base.py checks only the original hostname against a regex before urllib follows redirects, leaving its claimed private-network protection incomplete.

reads.best: Extensive session-management UI and cross-client state address everyday Hermes workflow friction, backed by broad frontend and backend tests.
reads.worst: The pinned sampler directly reads Claude Code .credentials.json outside Hermes secret routes and relies on many private core interfaces, despite disclosing those deviations.

reads.best: Turns the pet into an actionable job monitor using session-qualified runtime reads, read-only Kanban queries and explicit confirmation before stopping work.
reads.worst: No tests are shipped at the pinned commit despite nontrivial polling, session ownership, stale-state and interruption logic.

reads.best: No network calls, shell commands, or credentials at all; opens Hermes's own kanban/cron/session databases strictly read-only (mode=ro, query_only pragma), and the README is candid about its own limitations and past bugs found via backtesting.
reads.worst: The underlying feature category (time estimation for work queues) is fairly common, and there is no visual/UI polish (no screenshots, no desktop UI) despite thorough text documentation.

reads.best: The read-score-reread-human-gate workflow directly addresses silent OCR errors instead of merely exposing an OCR endpoint.
reads.worst: The useful local document pipeline has substantial external model, GPU, and service setup complexity, while the hosted path remains a remote dependency.

reads.best: A valuable approval-hook integration that models shell and PowerShell target expansion rather than trusting a command description.
reads.worst: Relative targets use the process cwd rather than the terminal session cwd, and missing targets pass the added guard; ownership also treats edits as creations and is not session-filtered ([resolver policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/policy.py), [ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/ledger.py), [write hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/__init__.py)).

reads.best: Middleware makes Hermes persistent-context changes inspectable, strips display fields from model requests and tests profile/session isolation and deletion.
reads.worst: The README supplies no installation walkthrough, click-to-revert is still TODO, and stored full diffs remain visible to compaction despite conversational-request cleanup.

reads.best: A compact, well-isolated sandbox (minimal env, memory cap, hard kill, call budget) that gives the model a real orchestration runtime, with 12 tests.
reads.worst: Tool dispatch runs synchronously in the parent with no deadline, so a slow or approval-waiting tool can run far past the 120 s timeout, and all MCP tools are exposed by default.

reads.best: A complete Desktop experience joins strict panel validation, traceable local calculations and user-confirmed data changes with tests of the planning boundaries.
reads.worst: Planning lacks medication and condition context, and a separate challenger call is not guaranteed to use a different model, limiting the safety and independence claims.

reads.best: Native hooks and an optional memory provider combine hierarchical wiki recall with automatic daily transcript capture and extensive edge-case tests.
reads.worst: Lookups send unredacted conversation context to OpenRouter and can add roughly twenty seconds per turn, while installation needs a documented workaround to avoid replacing the existing memory provider.

reads.best: The [profile compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierrem57/hermes-ikigai/59f405f8b98c2f0ecb4a29fe90322c76ea47ce95/core.py) preserves unrelated memory entries, fits its additions to the character budget, and excludes inferred and local-only answers from compiled profiles.
reads.worst: In [interview_turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierrem57/hermes-ikigai/59f405f8b98c2f0ecb4a29fe90322c76ea47ce95/core.py), tagged widget replies skip the session-ownership check, so a matching tagged reply from another chat can alter the active interview.

reads.best: Retention is explicit, sequential and metadata-verified, with tested timeout and late-handle cleanup instead of invented readiness metrics.
reads.worst: It retains connections rather than agent or tool memory, and neither switching-speed gains nor per-profile resource costs are established.

reads.best: Puts rules at the point of need, with compound triggers and a demo video and dashboard.
reads.worst: The repo is cluttered with one-off stage migration scripts, the manifest has no author, and many top-level test files hold no test functions.

reads.best: Broad, well-tested tools with a polished Desktop page and dashboard.
reads.worst: It is a grab-bag of common utilities rather than one new capability.

reads.best: A clean image-generation provider that reads GMI_API_KEY through Hermes's secret scope and is tested offline against a fake GMI server.
reads.worst: Every call spends the user's GMI credits with no Hermes approval prompt (disclosed in the README), and it is one more hosted image provider rather than a new idea.

reads.best: Careful launcher that never downloads, a clear privacy account and skill rules that payment happens only on request, with Hermes approval.
reads.worst: Moves money through an external npm wallet whose code is not in the repo, setup is manual, no Mac, and the README says it was lightly tested.

reads.best: Read-only SQLite access (mode=ro, 2-second timeout) with a privacy default that limits messaging chats to their own profile, plus privacy tests.
reads.worst: Detection is a heuristic on English and Indonesian phrasing, and with no tools or hooks it is a reporting command only.

reads.best: Ledger citation checks, coded absence-score limits, source failures and a persistent Desktop/HTML trail make brainstorming more inspectable than a free-form prompt.
reads.worst: Citation checks establish ledger membership rather than truth, and demand ratings and absence rulings still depend on the proposing model and incomplete default search coverage.

reads.best: A clean native web-search provider: the key comes from Hermes's secret store, it uses only the standard library, and its tests mock the network.
reads.worst: One more paid search backend, with search only (no extract).

reads.best: Separates model capture and checkpoint tools from user status controls and tests cap handling, stale notices, and tampered Markdown.
reads.worst: The advertised hard gate uses best-effort tool-name and command-text matching that can miss indirect registry writes; the JSON registry also lacks cross-process locking.

reads.best: Scoped-key handling, redirect refusal, bounded automatic classification and detailed tests support a well-documented provider integration.
reads.worst: Most model selection happens in a proprietary external service, and routing preferences are shared across every chat on the profile.

reads.best: Evidence-bound design: the model can't write copy or HTML, records are signed, 232 tests, and a sandboxed browser subprocess with SSRF blocking and timeouts.
reads.worst: Narrow audience with heavy setup (Node, Playwright, Chromium) and strict model-route rules; the README is dense jargon with no screenshots, and approval is an agent-callable tool.

reads.best: Uses skill lifecycle hooks for drift detection that a skill alone cannot do.
reads.worst: Very large, abstract codebase whose value to ordinary users is hard to see.

reads.best: Automatic checkpoint evidence and recovery reminders address real continuity problems without network services.
reads.worst: Although recovery briefings filter by sender, sessionguard_status and /guard read all profile checkpoints without sender filtering, exposing other users' work on a shared gateway.

reads.best: A clear Desktop approval pane, practice flow, expiring proposals and tested concurrent rejection preserve a useful human-review step without holding wallet keys.
reads.worst: get_trade_status rebuilds aged approved transactions without rechecking quote drift, so a later wallet handoff can escape the price-change tolerance checked at approval.

reads.best: Broad surface (Desktop, Telegram, chat commands) with changelog, security policy and honest scope limits.
reads.worst: Selection of what to save is manual (/shelf add), file-type and size limits apply, and I could not confirm test coverage or hooks from the docs.

reads.best: A small standard-library implementation adds replay protection, sender lockouts and scoped-secret lookup without replacing Hermes approvals.
reads.worst: The guard explicitly allows protected tools when session identity is absent or evicted, so its security boundary fails open on missing lifecycle context.

reads.best: A large real test suite (161 test functions) exercises the actual token-resolution, contrast-math and consent-tracking logic, not stubs.
reads.worst: Core code is written in a very dense, unidiomatic style (long chained statements, giant nested ternaries) that hurts readability and maintainability.

reads.best: The result-transform hook changes what reaches the agent, with deterministic masking, content hashes and a bounded host-model reviewer ([hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/__init__.py), [reviewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/reviewer.py)).
reads.worst: After local secret masking it sends the original raw output to the reviewer, then persists the reviewer dictionary including cleaned_text, instruction snippets and _raw_text, undermining the before-model masking and metadata-only privacy claims ([hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/__init__.py), [reviewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/reviewer.py)).

reads.best: Clear setup and disclosure, gives Hermes real access to the user's own health data.
reads.worst: No code in the plugin itself; credentials are stored by the npm package locally rather than in Hermes's secret store.

reads.best: Cautious design: dry-run default, symlink and containment checks, sensitive files never moved.
reads.worst: Desktop pane is a static stub and tests are thin.

reads.best: Cryptographic integer-weight draws share a tested persistent store with an animated Desktop pane and terminal rendering.
reads.worst: The practical benefit is narrow, and the store explicitly drops advisory locking on Windows.

reads.best: Automatic, bounded due-item injection and a durable archive keep obligations visible across conversations ([code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zzzubair/hermes-agenda/d5a34a747d5d6e98cd2e398514544db6fa9d41a1/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: There are no tests, read/modify/write operations have no lock, and reminder subprocess failures return None while adding the task can still report success ([code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zzzubair/hermes-agenda/d5a34a747d5d6e98cd2e398514544db6fa9d41a1/__init__.py)).

reads.best: The portable manifest marks its write-capable MCP server untrusted so Hermes can require human approval.
reads.worst: The repository contains no tool implementation or tests; the remote server and payment behavior are outside the pinned commit.

reads.best: A fun, working, hand-written arcade that uses dashboard, tools and slash command around one atomic score store.
reads.worst: No tests, the agent side is three trivial leaderboard queries, POST /scores accepts any score, and the README embeds none of its screenshots or demo gif.

reads.best: SymPy and factorization really run locally with no keys and no network.
reads.worst: Claims more than the code does (no Tate or 2-descent, torsion via an unchecked Lutz-Nagell test, '100% deterministic' primality), its parse timeout can't fire, and the README promotes a token.

reads.best: No key, no local code, and a clear data-handling section with an honest list of limits.
reads.worst: Essentially a marketing funnel to a hosted quiz endpoint (links are tagged for sign-up tracking); nothing here a URL bookmark plus a skill could not do.

reads.best: The small package clearly discloses remote calls, needs no credentials and marks the server untrusted.
reads.worst: There is no pinned server implementation or test suite, and the PR explicitly says the package has not been tested in Hermes.

reads.best: The package is transparent, small and safe by scope: remote read-only access, no key, no local execution and links back to source articles.
reads.worst: It is mostly a remote blog connector plus instructional skill, so a prompt/skill and ordinary web access cover much of the same value and there is little pinned implementation to test.

reads.best: Clear multi-client install docs with OAuth through a pinned mcp-remote version.
reads.worst: For Hermes it is only an mcp.json that runs npx (needing Node) and a skill, a niche data service with no Hermes-specific code or tests.

reads.best: It returns detection, validation and doctor reports alongside generated file lists, making scaffold failures inspectable. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994/tools.py)
reads.worst: Committed bytecode violates catalog rules, model-selected paths and names permit arbitrary writes, and validation installs dependencies without approval; the pin also lacks a README. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994/tools.py) [Pinned file list](https://api.github.com/repos/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/git/trees/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994?recursive=1)

reads.best: The worktree-and-diff workflow could make agent edits reviewable, and basic copy, apply and discard lifecycle tests are present.
reads.worst: The claimed sandbox is not enforced: middleware only rewrites existing cwd fields, leak/egress counts are hardcoded zero, and commit can report success and discard a shadow after git apply fails.

reads.best: The registered handler obtains run identity from a read-only lookup and refuses missing or ambiguous runs, with scoped credentials and comment-only writes.
reads.worst: The duplicate key includes summary text and exists only in memory, so changing the summary or restarting permits another comment for the same run despite the one-comment claim.

reads.best: The small manifest marks both remote MCP connections untrusted.
reads.worst: The submission is only declarative connector metadata, leaving the claimed hosted tools, payment path, and reliability outside reviewable code.

reads.best: The skill clearly handles midnight, equal times, invalid inputs and daylight-saving ambiguity without requesting health records ([skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlucwright/daygauge-agent-plugin/b1f9ef5844cb03f87a38a86cdf0dc05d70e182e0/skills/daygauge-sleep-midpoint/SKILL.md)).
reads.worst: The entire capability is arithmetic instructions for the model, with no executable calculator, app integration or outcome tests ([skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlucwright/daygauge-agent-plugin/b1f9ef5844cb03f87a38a86cdf0dc05d70e182e0/skills/daygauge-sleep-midpoint/SKILL.md)).

reads.best: Keyless, read-only hosted endpoint.
reads.worst: Essentially a sales funnel for a paid service that a prompt could replicate; no code.
